concepts.title: Monsoon Mechanism and Seasons of India
concepts.definition: India's climate is dominated by the monsoon mechanism of differential heating, ITCZ shift, jet streams and Tibetan plateau effects, giving four seasons of cold weather, hot weather, advancing monsoon and retreating monsoon with rainfall from the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches.
concepts.key_idea: The onset and retreat of the southwest monsoon, the burst of the monsoon, and October heat and retreating monsoon rains of Tamil Nadu shape the annual weather rhythm.

concepts.title: Rainfall Distribution, Variability and El Nino
concepts.definition: Rainfall in India varies from very high on the Western Ghats windward side and Meghalaya's Cherrapunji-Mawsynram to arid western Rajasthan, with the El Nino southern oscillation affecting monsoon strength and variability year to year.
concepts.key_idea: Areas receiving over 400 cm of rain contrast with below 60 cm zones, and this variability decides agriculture, water supply and flood-drought risk.

concepts.title: Climate, Monsoon Dependence and Its Variability
concepts.definition: India's climate is described as the monsoon type with alternating wet and dry seasons, and the economy from agriculture to water supply depends on the timing and variability of monsoon rains, so years of weak monsoon bring drought while strong monsoons bring floods.
concepts.key_idea: The southwest monsoon delivers about 75 to 80 per cent of annual rainfall in four months, making its variability the single most important climatic fact of India.
